doc.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Joining the Mangione Jazz Brothers
summary: After the Air Force and Eastman study, he joined Chuck and Gap Mangione at The Pythod; Nat Adderley heard them and got them signed to Riverside.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How did you get hooked up with the Jazz Brothers?

Chuck and Gap [Mangione]. Well after I came out of the service, you know I went into the Air Force and then I came back and I was studying at the Eastman School of Music with Bill Street, a percussion teacher there. And I started working at a place called The Pythod which was a local jazz club up there. And they had a lot of people coming through. And Chuck and Gap were local musicians and I think Chuck had the band. He was leading one of the local bands and working in this club. So I think shortly after I got home out of the Air Force, the drummer who was working there had left or something happened to him. And a couple of days later I just went in and played the gig. And we became friends. Actually I had known Chuck for a long time before I went into the service. But I started working that gig and we became friends. It was almost like family you know. His father had the Italian grocery store and the food and all that kind of stuff.
Didn’t he always invite the visiting musicians to Rochester over to his house?

Oh, yeah, yeah. And they would go in to the store and his mother would just put the pots on and everybody would eat. Well we’d play. And we’d stay over there and we’d play and everything. And then we, the group came, kind of worked together a lot and then we made a record. I think what happened is Nat Adderley I think heard about us. And Cannon had a series called “Cannonball Adderley Presents” at that time, from Riverside Records. And he signed us for Riverside and we did our first album.
It’s interesting that years later — but we’ll get to that.

Right. And I remember they came up to, not — I don’t think it was Cannon — but I think Nat came up to The Pythod and sat in the audience and listened to the band you know. And what happened from that is we wound up going to New York to play at the old Five Spot. There was two Five Spots at the time. The old one was in the Bowery and they it moved up around Sixth Avenue.
